title: Embed API tail-latency deep dive and runtime patch: dynamic microbatch allocator + kernel-select hints
creator: Maya Chen
description: Problem summary: Hosted embeddings endpoint shows persistent p99 tail spikes (observed ~350-500ms on production steady-state) for short-sequence traffic and mixed-length bursts. Root-cause signals from tracing and perf counters point to three correlated contributors: 1) microbatch packing variance causing small batches to execute inefficient kernels, 2) runtime kernel selector picking a safety/compatibility codepath for certain quantized weights causing ~2x per-token cost, and 3) intermittent KV cache misses that force cold attention-key recomputation on a subset of requests. This ticket captures the investigation and implements a low-risk runtime patch that (A) dynamically allocates microbatches by grouping requests by token-length buckets and approximate KV-cache locality, and (B) exposes a kernel-hinting API to prefer the fast FP16/INT8 path when model metadata indicates it is safe.
comments: 2026-02-21 - Maya Chen: Kicked off triage after ops alert. Captured traces for 48h and dumped p99 distribution per-host. Noticed host-level outliers align with higher variance in sequence length and occasional cache thundering when bursts hit new shards.

2026-02-24 - Rafael Ortega: Added microbench harness that replays production request sequences and measures scheduler decisions. Baseline p50/p95/p99 recorded: 28ms / 112ms / 412ms for model small-embed-v1 on g4dn-like hardware emulation.

2026-02-27 - Rafael Ortega: Profiling results attached in Confluence (link below). Kernel selection heatmap shows ~18% of microbatches falling back to compatibility kernel due to alignment of weight quant params. Those batches correlate with the worst tail cases.
2026-03-01 - Eng-Infra feedback from Priya Suresh: Suggested adding a quick feature-flagged rollout and metric dashboard for request grouping efficiency and kernel path usage before wide rollout.

2026-03-05 - Rafael Ortega: Implemented dynamic microbatch allocator prototype: groups requests into three length buckets (short, medium, long) and attempts n-1 opportunistic merges with same-kv-shard affinity. Local benchmarks: p99 reduced to 210ms (+/-12ms). p95 also improved to 86ms.
2026-03-08 - Code review: PR #rwd/inference/emb-mb-23812 requested changes around metrics tagging and a defensive timeout for merge waits. Fixed and pushed; CI green. Link to PR in links field.

2026-03-10 - Rafael Ortega: Added kernel-hinting API to expose preferred kernel variant based on model metadata. Hooked into model registry so only verified model variants will flip the hint. Synthetic run shows further p99 drop to ~170ms when both allocator + kernel-hint are enabled.

2026-03-11 - QA: Canary job on dedicated pool for customer X for 6 hours. Observed no regressions in throughput; token-cost delta within expected variance. One regression seen for an edge quantized model; rolled back hint for that model and filed ENG-23847.

2026-03-12 - Rafael Ortega: Preparing rollout plan and dashboard tiles (cost per-token, kernel-path ratio, microbatch-merge-rate, p99 per-model). Next: telemetry alert thresholds and staggered canary to hosted API.
acceptance_criteria: p99 for embeddings endpoint (small-embed-v1) reduced from baseline ~410ms to <= 200ms on benchmark harness
No >1% regression in p50 for any supported model during canary window
Feature flag controls both allocator and kernel-hint independently and can be toggled globally or per-model
Dashboard shows kernel-path split and microbatch merge-rate; alerts fire if merge-rate drops >30% or kernel-hint error rate >0.5%
Rollout runbook completed with automatic fallback to previous scheduler on anomaly
risks: Aggressive grouping could increase tail for very latency-sensitive single-request flows if waits are misconfigured
Kernel hints may accidentally enable fast paths for incompatible quantizations — mitigated by model registry gating and per-model opt-in
Telemetry sampling and tagging must be thorough or we will miss regressions in rare models; adding extra logs increases storage/cost
next_steps: Finish dashboard tiles and alert thresholds (obs: Dashboards#embedding-tail-23812)
Run 24h hosted canary against 10% of traffic with feature flag ON (staggered) and collect per-model p99/merge-rate/kpath stats
Coordinate with Solutions Eng to notify customers with strict latency SLOs before hosted rollout
Prepare postmortem template to capture any anomalies during canary and early ramp
